_note: ILLUSTRATIVE placeholder answers of Flex Power Modules for RC-1 (OPP-0003), written for the PoC demo (P-49 part B). Not real unit positions; no rating, certification or figure here is a verified fact.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: The solution delivers 800 VDC two-wire distribution to the racks inside the 1500 VDC limit, sized for 198 to 330 kW racks in each 20 MW deployment unit with a growth path to 570 kW per rack position.
answers.reason: Flex Power Modules covers the 800 VDC distribution and rack power only; the 13.8 kV site buses and 15 kV class equipment come from the medium-voltage lot, and the utility step-down above 100 kV is not in the Flex offer.
answers.next_steps: Confirm the medium-voltage interface with the switchgear lot at the first dialogue session.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: Our 800 VDC distribution stays inside the voltage band: no setpoint or average above 1500 VDC, with an 840 VDC overvoltage disconnect. The system uses IT or high-resistance grounding with insulation monitoring for first-fault detection, and we will supply the grounding, fault-current and personnel-safety analysis for our scope.
answers.conditions: The final grounding scheme is chosen with the Owner at the technical decision point.
answers.next_steps: Share the draft grounding analysis during dialogue.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: On the distribution side, our power distribution and tap cans support fast shutdown by shunt trip, current-limited DC fault current and two protection zones, with insulation monitoring on the facility side and residual current monitoring at the rack interface. Series arcing is covered by connector temperature monitoring and high-frequency sensing at the rack interface and converter outputs.
answers.reason: The L2.13 clause on the power blocks (shunt-trip shutdown, internal disconnect and a current-limiting stage in each block) belongs to the power blocks, which are not in the Flex offer (capability gap REQ-0003-0213).
answers.conditions: Clearing times and the holdup covering up to about 20 ms are stated in the tender data sheets; solid-state breaker ratings for liquid-cooled shelves are confirmed at the design review.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: At distribution and rack level the solution uses N+1 converters and semiconductor OR-ing so that no single failure drops a rack, supporting the 99.9% availability target.
answers.reason: The 4+1 power-block arrangement and its DC static transfer switch sit with the MV-to-800 VDC power blocks, which Flex does not offer in this bid; we cover the redundancy downstream of the blocks.
answers.next_steps: Agree the catcher-path interface with the power-block supplier the Owner selects.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: Rack power equipment is designed to UL 62368-1 methods with leakage held within 3.5 mA AC and 10 mA DC, and meets EMC Class A to CISPR 32 and CISPR 35. The rack-level capacitive storage follows the applicable storage safety standards.
answers.reason: Campus battery storage is not in the Flex offer, so the UL 9540A cell, module and rack fire propagation tests apply only where our rack-level capacitive storage falls in scope; that scope and the certification path are still to be confirmed.
answers.conditions: EMC test reports are provided at the factory test.
answers.next_steps: Confirm with the Owner which storage standards apply to rack-level capacitive storage.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: Rack-level capacitive energy storage and fast converter control hold the bus within plus or minus 3% with 3 ms settling for the reference load steps of up to 180% of rack TDP.
answers.conditions: Performance is confirmed by the system-level simulation accepted before delivery.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: Flex supplies 125 A 800 VDC power whips hardwired to the tap can behind a normally open contactor, so the whip is only live when the rack-side connector is locked.
answers.reason: Our qualified connectors do not have a latch switch built into the connector body.
answers.workaround: A pilot-contact loop in the connector opens the contactor before the latch can release and closes it only once locked, giving the same no-live-unplug and anti-arcing result.
answers.next_steps: Provide the interlock sequence and connector data for Owner review.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: Each compute rack takes an 800 VDC to 54 VDC power shelf; we will state the shelf output voltage and converter count in the tender against the six 15 kW converter baseline. Racks are designed for 198 to 330 kW with a liquid-cooled shelf path to 570 kW and native 800 VDC inside the rack, with local smoothing and solid-state branch protection.
answers.conditions: The 570 kW liquid-cooled shelf is offered for later phases and fixed at the technical decision point.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: For Phase 1 the solution offers 800 VDC power racks beside the compute racks, taking 415 to 480 VAC three-phase through 12 whips of 100 A for about 660 kW, with per-converter energy storage and the optional four-unit battery backup.
answers.reason: Our power rack is built from a larger standard rectifier than the 18.3 kW converter in the RFP.
answers.workaround: Shelves use our standard larger rectifiers, giving the same about 660 kW per rack and at least the 1,200 J storage per converter position with fewer, larger converters.
answers.next_steps: Show the rack layout and storage figures at the first dialogue session.

answers.reason: End-to-end efficiency includes upstream power conversion outside our scope, and the above-95% figure at 20% load still has to be shown by test for our part of the chain.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: We accept liquidated damages for missed service levels, capped by the at-risk amounts described, and delay penalties that scale with the length of the delay and the seriousness of the breach, subject to an aggregate cap on liquidated damages and delay penalties together.
answers.reason: Liquidated damages and delay penalties have no overall limit as written, which leaves an open-ended risk on a phased multi-lot delivery.
answers.workaround: An aggregate cap on liquidated damages and delay penalties together, set as a percentage of each lot's price; the percentage is stated in the financial offer and listed in the commercial exceptions schedule (CT-08).

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: Our commercial exceptions are listed in the separate exceptions schedule and kept to a minimum: on liquidated damages, only the aggregate cap per lot asked for under CT-07; any indexed price is shown there only as an alternative to the firm price.

Illustrative placeholder response: We provide a supply-chain security and risk plan for the components Flex designs and builds, with qualified alternatives for third-party semiconductors. Instead of a guarantee for each original component over the system's whole lifetime, we commit to the availability period stated as the proposed change.
answers.reason: No supplier can guarantee every original component for an open-ended system lifetime: electronic parts follow their makers' life cycles.
answers.workaround: Spare parts or compatible form-fit-function replacements available for at least 10 years from acceptance, with at least 12 months' notice of end of life and a last-time-buy offer before any component is discontinued.
